world.title: Has Trump turned the tables on Iran - or is another round of war coming?
world.summary: The Trump administration believes it has gained an advantage over Iran, citing the rerouting of maritime traffic through the Omani corridor and a global shift away from Persian Gulf oil. This assessment suggests that Tehran's influence may be waning. However, Iran remains largely unfazed by these developments, leaving questions about potential future conflicts unresolved.

world.title: Prince Harry, Meghan returning to U.K. with their children, says British newspaper
world.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan are returning to the United Kingdom with their children, according to British media reports. However, the couple will not resume their roles as working members of the royal family. This visit marks their continued separation from royal duties, following their previous decision to step back from official responsibilities within the monarchy.

world.title: Russia’s Fuel Crisis Hits Moscow as Rationing Spreads
world.summary: Russia is experiencing a renewed fuel shortage crisis, acknowledged by officials since late last week. The situation has worsened due to a prolonged drone campaign from Ukraine targeting oil refineries and industrial sites. Rationing measures are now spreading across Moscow, affecting various sectors, including online retail and private businesses, as the conflict continues to impact fuel availability.

business.title: OpenAI confirms ChatGPT is down as logins and signups fail
business.summary: OpenAI has confirmed a significant outage affecting ChatGPT, preventing users from signing in, creating accounts, or accessing previous conversations. The issue began around 8 PM ET on Wednesday, August 19, and is impacting users globally. OpenAI is working to resolve the problem, but no specific timeline for restoration has been provided at this time.

business.title: ET Exclusive: Elon Musk's Starlink reapplies for India approval of satellite network with direct-to-device tech
business.summary: Starlink has submitted a new application to India's space regulator for its Gen 2 satellite constellation, aiming to deploy nearly 30,000 satellites in low Earth orbit. The proposal features advanced capabilities, including direct-to-device connectivity. This move comes as India evaluates expanding satellite communication spectrum access and is in the process of finalizing regulations for satellite-based mobile services.

business.title: TrueFoundry's open source AI agent harness TrueForge boasts 30%-75% cheaper task completion than Claude Managed Agents
business.summary: TrueFoundry has launched an open-source AI agent called TrueForge, which reportedly completes tasks 30%-75% cheaper than Claude Managed Agents. The system provisions a sandbox only when code execution or file work is necessary, minimizing unnecessary compute usage. This development aims to enhance developer control over AI agents and tools while addressing cost concerns in enterprise settings.

technology.title: Public Exploit Code Released for Microsoft SCCM Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
technology.summary: Public proof-of-concept exploit code has been released for CVE-2026-47301, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM). This vulnerability could enable low-privileged domain users to gain SYSTEM access on Primary Site Servers. Organizations using SCCM are advised to assess their security measures to mitigate potential risks associated with this exploit.

technology.title: Morocco’s DGSSI Warns of Critical Apple Vulnerabilities
technology.summary: Morocco’s Directorate General of Information Systems Security (DGSSI) released a security bulletin on Tuesday, highlighting critical vulnerabilities in various Apple products. The advisory was issued as part of the agency's ongoing cyberattack monitoring efforts. Users are urged to take necessary precautions to protect their devices and data from potential threats associated with these vulnerabilities.

technology.title: I am unable to switch from Google to the Proton ecosystem because of this single app
technology.summary: A user expressed difficulty transitioning from Google to the Proton ecosystem due to reliance on a specific app. Despite appreciating Proton's clean, privacy-focused applications and the ecosystem's growth, the user found that one essential app was not available, hindering their ability to fully replace Google services. This limitation has prevented a complete switch to Proton's offerings.

sports.title: Five minutes, 28 covers, 300 tyres: How Galle's 130-member groundstaff beat the rain
sports.summary: At Galle International Cricket Stadium, a 130-member groundstaff efficiently covered the pitch after the first Test match between India and Sri Lanka. Despite the match concluding, the team managed to deploy 28 covers and 300 tyres in just five minutes to protect the field from rain. Their swift actions ensured the ground remained prepared for future play.

sports.title: Philadelphia Union vs. Inter Miami Lineups & Confirmed Team News for MLS Match
sports.summary: Inter Miami will face the Philadelphia Union in an MLS match at Subaru Park in Pennsylvania. Currently, Inter Miami ranks second in the Eastern Conference with 38 points after 19 games. The match is part of the ongoing MLS season, which features various teams competing for playoff positions. Lineups and team news have been confirmed ahead of the game.

sports.title: FIFA 2026 tech to be used for Afghanistan-India T20I series
sports.summary: FIFA World Cup 2026 production technology will be utilized for the upcoming three-match T20I series between Afghanistan and India in New Delhi. This marks the first instance of a bilateral cricket series being produced to the full host-broadcast standards set by FIFA. ITW Universe, which holds the broadcasting rights, aims to enhance the viewing experience significantly.

health.title: Tan-kissed? Dermatologists warn viral push for deeper tans is UV damage, not a beauty boost
health.summary: Dermatologists are cautioning against the viral trend of "tanmaxxing," which promotes achieving a deeper tan through increased sun exposure. Experts emphasize that this practice leads to harmful UV damage rather than enhancing beauty. The trend, popularized online, encourages individuals to prioritize a darker complexion, raising concerns about the long-term health risks associated with excessive sun exposure and skin damage.

health.title: The Best Time to Eat for Gut Health
health.summary: Experts emphasize the importance of consistent meal times for optimal gut health, highlighting the impact on metabolism, sleep, and blood sugar levels. Disrupted routines during summer can lead to "metabolic jet lag," affecting overall well-being. To maintain balance, individuals are encouraged to establish regular eating schedules, avoiding irregular meal times that can arise from seasonal changes and social activities.

health.title: How we found a new transmissible cancer in bullhead catfish
health.summary: Scientists from the U.S. Geological Survey and the Vermont Fish and Wildlife Department discovered a new transmissible cancer in brown bullhead catfish in Lake Memphremagog. Anglers have reported catching fish with distinctive black lesions for over a decade. The research highlights the cancer's spread among fish populations, raising concerns about its impact on local ecosystems and fisheries.

science.title: Australian redback spiders' mating somersault may be driven by more than one gene
science.summary: A study published on August 12 reveals that the mating ritual of the Australian redback spider, where the male flips toward the female's fangs, may be influenced by multiple genes. This behavior, which appears to invite cannibalism, highlights the complexity of mating strategies in this species. Researchers suggest genetic factors play a significant role in this unsettling ritual.

science.title: The dawn of artificial photosynthesis: how scientists created an unmanned solar-to-fuel converter that adapts to the weather
science.summary: Researchers have developed an unmanned solar-to-fuel converter that autonomously produces liquid formic acid from water and carbon dioxide, adapting to varying sunlight conditions. This innovative device operates without batteries or control electronics, addressing the challenges posed by fluctuating solar energy. The technology aims to enhance efficiency in chemical reactions, overcoming the instability of sunlight reaching the Earth's surface.

science.title: University of Birmingham develops "switchable smart gel" that could revolutionise targeted drug delivery
science.summary: Researchers at the University of Birmingham have developed a "switchable smart gel" that transitions between gel and liquid states when exposed to ultraviolet light or acid. This multi-responsive material features acid-triggered release mechanisms, potentially enabling targeted drug delivery to diseased tissues. The innovation may enhance treatment efficacy by allowing precise control over drug release in specific areas.
